evaluation_scope.claim_boundary: Retain decision evidence based on recorded triad outputs plus validated real-use dogfood pilots. This does not claim every future refinement will pass without fresh evidence.

criteria.name: repo-specific existing capability lookup
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline gives the right generic reuse direction but does not identify the actual existing review skill path.

criteria.name: artifact-level routing evidence
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline does not tie the routing decision to concrete downstream contracts.

criteria.name: route-conflict risk handling
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline warns about duplication but is weaker on why route conflict is the governing failure mode.

criteria.name: read-only decision boundary
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline asks for confirmation but gives a less auditable read-only basis for the decision.

scenarios.outcome_signal: Current arm makes the right route decision and anchors it in actual repo artifacts.
scenarios.rationale: Both arms avoid premature creation; current is retain-grade because it proves the existing carrier and protects the routing boundary.

criteria.name: quality standard integration
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline names quality dimensions but gives less explicit skill-refiner flow ownership.

criteria.name: real-scene calibration
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline says real cases are needed but does not bind them as clearly to the intake gate.

criteria.name: comparative validation design
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline suggests validation; current states a smaller with/without design suited to the scenario.

criteria.name: owner routing
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline is less explicit about not routing to skill-creator until a new-skill gap is proven.

scenarios.outcome_signal: Current arm converts external-practice concern into a bounded refinement and validation gate.
scenarios.rationale: The output preserves skill-refiner ownership while preventing external-practice content from becoming abstract checklist noise.

criteria.name: ability matrix before file split
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline asks for a routing matrix but does not make ability ownership as concrete.

criteria.name: partial handoff to creator
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline holds everything under refinement and does not identify the creator-owned subcase.

criteria.name: completion gate discrimination
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline avoids edits, but current more precisely rejects a wrong completion-gate diagnosis.

criteria.name: consumer/routing risk
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline gives the risk but less sharply ties it to downstream consumer routing.

scenarios.outcome_signal: Current arm separates routing, refinement, and creator responsibilities instead of treating split as a file operation.
scenarios.rationale: This is the exact retain-critical behavior: prevent a plausible but premature structural edit.

criteria.name: human decision for ambiguous domain
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline stays with skill-refiner but does not name the need for human boundary decision.

criteria.name: ability matrix path
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline proposes strategy, while current produces a smaller pre-edit matrix gate.

criteria.name: creator boundary protection
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline says do not default to creation but is weaker on when creator is allowed.

criteria.name: no abstract best-practice rewrite
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline rejects abstract best-practice rewrite, but current makes it the central failure mode.

scenarios.outcome_signal: Current arm refuses a vague rewrite and routes the ambiguity to boundary discovery.
scenarios.rationale: Retain requires this behavior because vague rewrite requests are where skill-refiner can otherwise create expensive noise.

criteria.name: explicit adjacent-skill diagnosis
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline identifies the same skills but less explicitly frames the governing diagnosis.

criteria.name: routing matrix as required artifact
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline recommends a matrix; current makes it the central gate before editing.

criteria.name: human decision escalation
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline does not identify when a boundary conflict needs human decision.

criteria.name: quality standard gate
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline gives the right direction but less strongly requires quality-standard alignment before edits.

scenarios.outcome_signal: Current arm handles adjacent-skill conflict as routing governance, not wording preference.
scenarios.rationale: This directly protects the repo from trigger drift and ownership damage, which is the retain-level value of skill-refiner.

criteria.name: residue surface coverage
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline lists surfaces but current turns them into a residue audit gate.

criteria.name: consumer validation before deletion
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline warns about consumers; current makes consumer proof part of the deletion decision.

criteria.name: result evidence requirement
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline requires verification but does not require the structured result artifact.

criteria.name: owner classification
criteria.baseline_gap: Baseline classifies the task correctly, while current adds clearer owner consequences.

scenarios.outcome_signal: Current arm prevents destructive cleanup until reference surfaces and consumers are proven safe.
scenarios.rationale: The output is retain-grade because it converts deletion pressure into verifiable residue governance.

real_use_pilots.scope: Current v3 structured result for the skill-refiner triad audit and retain-gate closure work.
Self-dogfood final-operation gate proving the skill blocks premature create/retain decisions.
Dogfood drift gate proving user-superseded operation changes are persisted before edits.
External-practice shadow run proving all rings carry official/GitHub/community/local/user-context sources.
